story.originalTitle: Who slept worst last night: George Russell
story.summaryEn: The columnist argues that George Russell, despite finishing second on the podium at the Italian GP, should have won the race and therefore is this edition's subject of 'who slept worst last night'.
detailZh: 昨晚谁睡得最差：乔治·拉塞尔
这位英国车手在意大利大奖赛领奖台的第二级上昂首挺立，但这本应是一场他能赢下的比赛
我在这篇专栏里挑选写作对象时，尽量比单纯地问“谁在最近的大奖赛上过得最惨”更有想象力一些。毕竟，我可不想每周都写兰斯·斯特罗尔之流，把读者烦到无聊。
所以我原本并没打算写乔治·拉塞尔。在铃鹿和巴塞罗那之后，我的同行们今年已经让他两次睡不好觉了。然而这一次，我实在没法绕开他。尽管有那么一刻，我本想把目标换成弗拉维奥·布里亚托利，起因是他在周五的车队领队新闻发布会上那场古怪的亮相。
如果布里亚托利真心认为其中一位上诉法官存在偏袒，那倒也说得过去。但是，在国际汽联的新闻发布会上，把这样严重的指控抛进公共舆论场，在此过程中让国际汽联和迈凯伦都承受最大可能的声誉损害——抱着“总有一点能沾上”的心态——这种做事风格，即便在一级方程式这个弱肉强食的环境里，也已经不符合2026年的道德标准了。
我非常确定，如果角色互换，像安德烈亚·斯特拉这样有风度的人，会先在更私密的场合提出这类阴谋论，然后再去寻求最大程度的公开曝光。
不过算了。弗拉维奥就是弗拉维奥，他一生的事业无可争议，像我这样无足轻重的键盘侠或许应该感到庆幸：在一支日益同质化的一级方程式围场里，像他这样的人物依然存在。无论是好是坏。我要强调：我这么说完全没有讽刺的意思。真的。
如果你想象一个没有基米·安东内利的平行宇宙，这位28岁车手的生活本来会一切安好。他是那一代实力格外强劲的二级方程式（Formula 2）车手中最耀眼的一位，那一届车手里还有一位兰多·诺里斯——而他恰好是现任一级方程式世界冠军。正如预测的那样，梅赛德斯在新规则下打造出了整体最强的套件，拉塞尔本可以轻松领跑积分榜，并顺利走向他期待已久的最终加冕世界冠军之路。
因为这位现年20岁的意大利车手在蒙扎赛场上穿越车阵的惊人表现，对拉塞尔来说是一个分水岭式的时刻，而我认为他如今才刚刚开始意识到这一点。
赛后国际汽联新闻发布会上有一个瞬间，让人窥见了这一点。安东内利当时甚至还没有到场，还在为各家电视台一连串地接受夺冠车手的胜利采访，而拉塞尔和获得第三名的马克斯·维斯塔潘已经坐在蒙扎围场后方那间通常用作国际汽联赛后官方媒体发布会的空调房间里了。
主持人汤姆·克拉克森指出拉塞尔如今落后66分，并询问这位梅赛德斯车手如何评估自己在2026年仍有机会逆转夺冠的可能性。拉塞尔变得若有所思。他说了诸如“基米确实掌握着主动权”、“我甚至没有去想什么反击”之类的话，并表示要扭转局势将会“异常艰难”。
乔治·拉塞尔最终获得第二名，仅次于队友基米·安东内利，后者从第19位发车。
而且，最重要的是：“我只是接受了事情就是这样，从现在开始我只会享受它，并尽可能赢得更多的比赛。”
几乎每一位车手的基因深处都刻着一种信念：自己是最伟大、最优秀的。即使外界得出了完全不同的结论，车手们也习惯于为失败寻找解释，以保住自己心中的那个版本的真相。
“没错，是别人赢了。但如果这个、那个以及其他种种因素对我来说稍有不同，一切本来会完全不同。”
拉塞尔的问题在于：在蒙扎，他从始至终都完成了一份几乎无可挑剔的工作。他没有犯任何实质性的错误，没有被车队坑害，也没有成为任何外部不利因素的受害者。甚至不在虚拟安全车（VSC）下进站的决定，客观上也是合理的——那个决定一度让比赛重新燃起了悬念，因为拉塞尔至少在一段时间内，在与安东内利的“悠悠球”式攻防拉锯中稳住了阵脚。
当一切都剥去之后，剩下的是：在那蒙扎公园历史性的周日，没有任何事情、没有任何人能够阻止安东内利。
这是那种能把麦粒与谷壳分开、真正伟大事业开始萌发的特殊日子。就像1984年的蒙特卡洛与塞纳、1992年的斯帕与迈克尔·舒马赫，或者2016年的英特拉格斯与维斯塔潘一样。
安东内利的表现如此出色，以至于就连拉塞尔身上那股车手固有的基因，即使全力进入自我防御模式，也无法再为“另一辆车里的那个人在不同情况下本有可能被击败”这一说法找到任何说得通的解释了。
不止一位F1评论员将基米·安东内利与埃尔顿·塞纳相提并论。
这或许就是拉塞尔必须正视现实的时候了：只要他还与这位无忧无虑的意大利人同队，他在这项赛车运动巅峰中举起世界冠军奖杯这一毕生梦想，就将会非常、非常难以实现。而这名意大利车手的天赋，如今不仅罗斯伯格拿他与塞纳相提并论，其他人也开始这样认为。
然而，恰恰是罗斯伯格的故事，为拉塞尔在视野中保留了最后一丝希望。
2015年底，几乎已经没有人相信这位德国车手还能在同等赛车的条件下打破刘易斯·汉密尔顿的统治。我自己当时也曾写道，罗斯伯格恐怕永远成不了世界冠军。我错了。
在历史背景下，很少有专家会说罗斯伯格比汉密尔顿更有天赋。七座世界冠军奖杯本身就说明了一切。但在2015年底，罗斯伯格退后一步、向内审视，不知怎的设法将自己能力的极限又往前推了一点——到了2016年，凭借一场令人难忘的毅力壮举，再加上一点往往眷顾有付出之人的运气，他最终还是成为了F1世界冠军。
也许拉塞尔应该邀请罗斯伯格喝一杯蓝布鲁斯科葡萄酒，问问他当初到底是怎么做到的。
因为非凡的成就需要非凡的表现，而罗斯伯格在职业生涯中至少成功做到过一次。在种种不利之下。
毫无疑问，拉塞尔是他这一代最出色的车手之一。在未来一两年内，我们将知道这是否已经足够。
一级方程式的历史上充满了从未成为世界冠军的杰出天才。例如斯特林·莫斯、罗尼·彼得森、斯特凡·贝洛夫，或者更近一些的让·阿莱西和胡安·巴勃罗·蒙托亚。
乔治·拉塞尔的职业生涯会不会与詹卡洛·菲谢凯拉的轨迹相似？
同为意大利人的詹卡洛·菲谢凯拉多年来也被视为一位杰出的天才。2004/05年冬天，当他的雷诺车队终于给他提供了一辆有夺冠能力的赛车时，我为一家印刷杂志撰写了封面故事——一篇赛季前瞻，聚焦世界冠军的主要争夺者。
杂志出版后，菲谢凯拉当时的经纪人恩里科·扎纳里尼给我打来电话。他非常愤怒，因为登上封面的偏偏是菲谢凯拉当时的队友费尔南多·阿隆索，而后者在那时还基本是个无名之辈。而且，菲谢凯拉也没能进入展示其他夺冠热门的较小图片之列，我们在那里选择的是舒马赫和基米·莱科宁这样的车手。
最终，阿隆索真的成为了世界冠军。而菲谢凯拉则以一个永恒的、未能兑现的天才，而非冠军的身份，留在了大奖赛的历史中。
拉塞尔如今发现自己也处在类似的境地。
二十年后的我们回顾今天，会看到一个像菲西凯拉那样的职业生涯——天赋出众，却终究没有冠军头衔吗？还是说拉塞尔能找到出路，最终成为又一个罗斯伯格？
如果做不到，我编辑部的一位同事昨天的玩笑可能就会应验：“很快拉塞尔就会去当采访者，接替大卫·库特哈德。一样的职业路线。”
不过，有一件事是任何人都无法从拉塞尔身上夺走的。
从体育角度来看，他或许可以算是2026年意大利大奖赛的失意者之一。但从人情层面来看，他是周日午后最大的赢家之一。
拉塞尔承认他的队友"表现极其出色"
即便他在颁奖台上为安东内利鼓掌的必要环节中显得有些拘谨，也不会有人为此责怪他。毕竟，他刚刚经历了赛车生涯中最令人痛苦的难堪时刻之一。
但拉塞尔以绅士的风度承受了嘘声和口哨声——意大利观众其实本不该发出这些声音——展现出了他作为一名优秀运动员的风范。
detailEn: Who slept worst last night: George Russell
The Briton held his head high on the second step of the Italian GP podium, but it was a race he should have won

I try to choose my subjects for this column a little more imaginatively than simply asking who had the worst time at the most recent grand prix. After all, I do not want to bore our readers by writing about Lance Stroll & Co. every single week.

That is why I had not really intended to write about George Russell. After Suzuka and Barcelona, colleagues of mine have already made him sleep badly twice this year. And yet, this time, I simply cannot look past him. Even though, for a moment, I was tempted to take on Flavio Briatore instead, after his bizarre appearance in Friday's team principals' press conference.

If Briatore genuinely believes that one of the appeal judges was biased, fair enough. But to throw an allegation of that magnitude into the public arena of an FIA press conference, maximising the potential reputational damage to both the FIA and McLaren in the process - in the spirit of "something will stick" - is a style of doing business that, even in Formula 1's shark tank, no longer fits the ethical standards of 2026.

I am quite sure that, had the roles been reversed, a gentleman such as Andrea Stella would have raised conspiracy theories of that kind in a more private setting first, before seeking the maximum possible level of publicity.

But never mind. Flavio is Flavio, his life's work is beyond dispute, and insignificant keyboard warriors such as myself should probably be grateful that, in an increasingly homogenised Formula 1, characters like him still exist. For better or worse. And I stress: I mean that entirely without irony. Really.

If you imagine a parallel universe without Kimi Antonelli, life would be perfectly fine for the 28-year-old. He was the standout driver of an exceptionally strong Formula 2 generation that also featured a certain Lando Norris, who just happens to be the reigning Formula 1 world champion. Mercedes, as predicted, has developed the strongest overall package under the new regulations, Russell would be leading the championship comfortably, and he would be well on his way to finally becoming world champion.
Because the now 20-year-old Italian's extraordinary charge through the field at Monza was a watershed moment for Russell, and I think he is only just beginning to realise it.

There was a moment in the FIA press conference after the race that offered a glimpse of that. Antonelli had not even arrived yet, still working his way through one triumphant winner's interview after another for the television broadcasters, while Russell and third-placed Max Verstappen were already sitting inside the air-conditioned room at the back of the Monza paddock that usually serves as the setting for the FIA's official post-race media sessions.

Moderator Tom Clarkson pointed out Russell's now 66-point deficit and asked the Mercedes driver how he assessed his chances of somehow still becoming Formula 1 World Champion in 2026. Russell became reflective. He said things such as: "Definitely Kimi’s in control of it", "I'm not even thinking about a comeback", and that turning things around would be "exceptionally challenging".
George Russel came second to team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who started 19th
And, above all: "I’m just sort of accepting that it is what it is and I’m just going to enjoy it from here on in and try and win as many races as possible."

It is deeply embedded in the DNA of almost every racing driver to believe that he is the greatest and the best. Even when the outside world reaches an entirely different conclusion, racing drivers have a habit of finding explanations for defeat that preserve their own version of reality.
"Yes, the other guy won. But if this, that and the other had gone just a little differently for me, everything would have been completely different."

Russell's problem is this: At Monza, he did an almost optimal job from start to finish. He made no meaningful mistakes, he was not sabotaged by his team, and he did not fall victim to any external circumstances. Even the call not to pit under the VSC, which briefly injected fresh momentum into the race as Russell managed, for a while at least, to hang on in his yo-yo battle with Antonelli, was objectively a logical one.
What remains, when everything else is stripped away, is this: Nothing and nobody could have stopped Antonelli on that historic Sunday in the Parco di Monza.

It was one of those special days on which the wheat is separated from the chaff and something genuinely great begins to grow. Like Monte Carlo 1984 with Ayrton Senna, Spa 1992 with Michael Schumacher, or Interlagos 2016 with Verstappen.

Antonelli's performance was so exceptional that even Russell's racing-driver DNA, operating in full self-defence mode, could no longer come up with a plausible explanation for how the guy in the other car might somehow have been beatable under different circumstances.
Kimi Antonelli has been compared to Ayrton Senna by more than one F1 pundit

This may be the point at which Russell has to confront the possibility that fulfilling his lifelong dream of lifting the World Championship trophy in the pinnacle of motorsport is going to be very, very difficult for as long as he shares a team with this carefree Italian, whose natural talent Nico Rosberg is now not alone in comparing with Senna's.
And yet, it is precisely Rosberg's story that offers Russell perhaps the last silver lining on the horizon.

At the end of 2015, there were very few people left who believed the German could still break Lewis Hamilton's supremacy in equal machinery. I myself wrote at the time that Rosberg would probably never become world champion. I was wrong.

There are very few experts who, in the historical context, would describe Rosberg as the greater talent than Hamilton. Seven world championship titles tell their own story. But at the end of 2015, Rosberg went away, looked inward, somehow managed to move the limits of his own ability a little further – and in 2016, through a memorable feat of determination and with a little of the luck that tends to favour the deserving, he became Formula 1 world champion after all.
Perhaps Russell should invite Rosberg for a glass of Lambrusco and ask him how exactly he managed it.
Because extraordinary achievements require extraordinary performances, and Rosberg managed to produce one at least once in his career. Against all odds.
There can be no doubt that Russell is one of the best drivers of his generation. Over the next year or two, we will find out whether that is enough.

Formula 1 history is full of exceptional talents who never became world champion. Stirling Moss, for example. Ronnie Peterson. Stefan Bellof. Or, in more recent times, Jean Alesi and Juan Pablo Montoya.
Could George Russell's career mirror that of Giancarlo Fisichella?

Giancarlo Fisichella, a fellow Italian, was also regarded for many years as an outstanding talent. In the winter of 2004/05, when his Renault team had finally given him a car capable of winning, I wrote the cover story for a print magazine – a season preview featuring the leading contenders for the world championship.

After the magazine came out, Fisichella's then-manager Enrico Zanarini called me. He was furious because, of all people, Fisichella's team-mate Fernando Alonso, still largely an unknown quantity at the time, had made it onto the cover. Nor, for that matter, had Fisichella made it into the smaller images featuring the other championship candidates, where we had instead chosen drivers such as Schumacher and Kimi Raikkonen.
In the end, Alonso really did become World Champion. And Fisichella went down in grand prix history not as a champion, but as an eternal, unfulfilled talent.
Russell now finds himself in a similar position.
When we look back in 20 years' time, will we see a career like Fisichella's – outstanding talent, but ultimately no title? Or will Russell find a way through and become a Rosberg after all?
If not, one of my colleagues in the newsroom may turn out to have been right when he joked yesterday: "Soon it'll be Russell doing the interviews instead of David Coulthard. Same career path."
There is one thing, however, that nobody can take away from Russell.
Sportingly, he may have been one of the losers of the 2026 Italian Grand Prix. On a human level, he was one of the great winners of Sunday afternoon.
George Russell admitted his team-mate is "performing incredibly well"

Nobody would have held it against him had he been somewhat restrained during the obligatory applause for Antonelli on the podium. After all, he had just experienced one of the most painful humiliations of his motorsport career.
But Russell endured the boos and whistles - which the Italian crowd really could have done without - like a gentleman, and showed just what a fine sportsman he is.

detailZh: 丹尼尔·里卡多在美国大奖赛前夕的现场表演令F1粉丝感到惊喜
前F1车手丹尼尔·里卡多与音乐家罗布·贝尔德一起吹奏口琴，令粉丝感到惊喜
丹尼尔·里卡多，Drive to Survive第七季
赛车文化超越赛道。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计和那些让赛车不仅仅是一项运动的故事。
前一级方程式车手丹尼尔·里卡多在美国德克萨斯州奥斯汀的舞台上出现了一个惊喜。
这位澳大利亚人与歌手兼词曲作者罗布·贝尔德一起加入了福特赛车和Enchanté快闪活动，在周五晚上一起演奏他与美国大奖赛旅途中共创作的原创歌曲。
一位粉丝在Instagram上发布的表演视频，截至写作时已经获得了超过7000个赞。一位粉丝评论说：“这治愈了我心中的某一部分，”另一位粉丝补充说：“我敢打赌他上辈子要么是鲍勃·迪伦的兄弟，要么是个牛仔哈哈。我们爱你，丹尼尔。”
“在这个时候，没有人关心比赛。很高兴看到丹尼尔回来了，即使他不再赛车，”另一位粉丝写道，另一位粉丝写道：“作为一个音乐家和蜜獾粉丝，和丹尼·里卡多一起演奏是我的梦想。”
“我是说真的很长的一段路。沙漠、乡村小道、游泳洞，所有这些。说实话，我迫不及待了。”
这次长途旅行是推广新系列 Enchanté Collection 的活动之一，名为《长途》。这些新产品在奥斯汀的 Distribution Hall 的临时展位上出售，展位上还有食品、饮料、闪粉纹身和赛车模拟器。
里卡多也被看到在支持 小红牛 车队的车手利亚姆·劳森，作为新西兰人，他在 Esses Bazaar ATX 活动中担任主角，与利亚姆·劳森和朋友们一起在东第六街的 Inn Cahoots 举办车库音乐会，此次活动是为本周末的美国大奖赛做准备。
detailEn: Daniel Ricciardo surprises F1 fans with on-stage performance ahead of US GP
Former Formula 1 driver Daniel Ricciardo surprised fans with a harmonica performance alongside musician Rob Baird
Daniel Ricciardo , Drive to Survive Season 7
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
Former Formula 1 driver Daniel Ricciardo made a surprise appearance on stage in Austin, Texas, with American singer-songwriter Rob Baird.
The Australian joined Baird at the Ford Racing and Enchanté pop-up on Friday night to play harmonica on an original song he co-wrote with Baird during a road trip to the United States Grand Prix.

A fan video of the performance, posted on Instagram, had picked up more than 7000 likes by the time of writing. "This healed something in me," one fan commented, while another added: "I'm sure he was either Bob Dylan's brother or a cowboy in a previous life lol. We love you, Daniel."

"At this point, no one cares about the race. Glad to see Daniel back, even if he’s not racing," someone else posted, and another fan wrote: "As a musician and a honey badger fan, it would be a dream to play with Danny Ric."
"And I mean the lonnnng way. Desert, backroads, swimming holes, all of it. Not gonna lie, I can't wait."

The road trip was part of the promotion of the new Enchanté collection, The Long Road. The new products are being sold at a pop-up at Distribution Hall in Austin alongside food, drinks, flash tattoos and racing simulators.

Ricciardo was also spotted supporting Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson as the New Zealander headlined Garage Sessions with Liam Lawson and Friends as part of Esses Bazaar ATX, held at Inn Cahoots on East Sixth Street ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

detailZh: 尼科·胡肯伯格在美国大奖赛上被加布里埃尔·博特洛托恶作剧后颜面扫地
加布里埃尔·博特洛托在美国大奖赛期间的一次粉丝见面会上玩了一个意外的恶作剧，让他的奥迪车队队友笑得前仰后合
赛车文化超越赛道。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计和那些让赛车不仅仅是一项运动的故事
年轻的奥迪车手加布里埃尔·博特洛托在美洲赛道前与队友尼科·胡肯伯格走在一起时，对他进行了一次恶作剧。两位车手在奥斯汀观众的欢呼声中走出，巴西人拉下了队友的裤子。
这个时刻的视频已经迅速走红，展示了胡肯伯格在周五如何走上舞台，当时博尔特洛从后面抓住他的裤子并将其拉下，引发了观众的欢呼和笑声。这位德国人对此玩笑表示宽容，一边笑着一边整理好衣服。
这个恶作剧为博尔特洛艰难的周末带来了一些轻松。巴西人在周日美国大奖赛将从最后一排发车，因为奥迪为他提供的动力单元组件超出了分配额度。
博尔特洛和胡肯伯格自2025年以来一直是队友，当时车队还以萨博的身份参赛，尽管车队已被德国巨头奥迪接管，但他们成为了赛场上更为轻松的搭档之一。然而，车队在2026年很难获得积分。车队在车队积分榜上排名第八，积分为23分，胡肯伯格积13分，博尔特洛积10分。
博尔特洛在美国大奖赛周末赛前表示：“我在可靠性方面看到了很多改进。显然，我们在新加坡显然有一个问题，我们相信我们已经找到了原因。”
“这显然不是理想的情况，但与此同时，它发生的时候我并没有在前面真正地竞争，所以这让我对它稍微不那么沮丧。但我希望我们能够在接下来的赛季中没有任何重大问题，并且能够以最佳状态完成比赛和排位赛，驾驶我们能够驾驶的最好的汽车，从中提取一切。”
detailEn: Nico Hulkenberg left red-faced after Gabriel Bortoleto prank at United States GP
Gabriel Bortoleto left his Audi team-mate laughing after pulling an unexpected prank during a fan appearance at the United States Grand Prix
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.

Young Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto played a prank on his team-mate Nico Hulkenberg as the pair walked out in front of thousands of fans at the Circuit of the Americas. With both drivers walking out to cheers from the Austin crowds, the Brazilian pulled down his team-mate's trousers.

Videos of this moment have gone incredibly viral, showing Hulkenberg making his way onto the stage on Friday when Bortoleto grabbed his trousers from behind and pulled them down, to loud cheers and laughter from the crowd. The German took the joke in good humour, laughing as he pulled his clothes straight.

The prank offered some light relief on a tough weekend for Bortoleto. The Brazilian will start Sunday’s United States Grand Prix from the back of the grid, after Audi took him beyond his allocation of power unit components.

Bortoleto and Hulkenberg have been team-mates since 2025, when the team still raced as Sauber, and have formed one of the more light-hearted partnerships on the grid despite it being taken over by German giant Audi. The outfit has found points hard to come by in 2026, however. The team is eighth in the constructors’ championship on 23 points, with the experienced Hulkenberg on 13 and Bortoleto on 10.

"I have seen lots of improvement on reliability," Bortoleto said on Thursday ahead of the United States Grand Prix race weekend. "I think we had one [issue] in Singapore obviously, that we believe we found the reason of.

"It was obviously something not ideal to happen, but at the same time it happened when I was not really fighting at the front, so made me a little bit less upset about it. But I hope we are able to do the rest of the season without having any major issue and that we are able to just complete the races and qualifying in the best condition and the best car possible out there that we can drive and extract everything from it."

relatedItems.originalTitle: Why Cadillac F1 boss provoked fresh intrigue by dodging driver question
detailZh: 为什么凯迪拉克F1负责人通过回避车手问题引发新的好奇
关于瓦尔特里·博塔斯在凯迪拉克未来去向的猜测持续存在，因为车队正打算引入一名美国车手
马辛·布德科夫斯基，凯迪拉克车队负责人
美国大奖赛周末自然意味着聚光灯转向了F1的两支美国车队。这也导致凯迪拉克在对其2027年及以后车手阵容的猜测中面临了一些尴尬的问题。
Sergio Perez和Valtteri Bottas都签订了“多年”合同，据说是所谓的“一年加一年”安排，其中第二年是否续约是可选的，取决于双方满足各种条件。两位车手之间的表现差异如此之大，以至于Bottas的位置已经成为了几个月来车队的八卦话题。
最近任命的团队负责人Marcin Budkowski已经不得不对此进行一些灭火工作，他的前任Graeme Lowdon也是如此。但周五在奥斯汀举行的FIA车队代表新闻发布会上的一个相当奇特的时刻表明，凯迪拉克的计划并不像之前宣传的那样固定。
引发这一事件的催化剂是来自一位广播员的关于Perez即将迎来第300场大奖赛起跑的软问题：“评价一个在网格后部战斗的车手有多难，同时他给人的印象是比队友有更好的赛季表现？关于车手，你们有兴趣就也许的预备角色与Esteban [奥康]进行任何对话吗？”
在试图给出一个合适的含糊其辞的答案时，Budkowski开始感到困惑。
“看，对于一个像Checo这样的车手，正如你所说，他有着丰富的经验和许多比赛，我可以告诉你，他并不像任何接近退休的车手那样表现或驾驶，”他说。
“他在驾驶座上非常努力。他在幕后也非常努力地推动我们，在简报室和外面，他经常给我和其他团队成员发短信，推动我们进步。他渴望胜利，他充满动力，这实际上是非常好的。他以自己的风格做到这一点。
“我们有两名车手：一个可能更热情，另一个可能更冷静，如果我们可以这样说的。他们都以自己独特的方式推动车队，但Checo确实是在非常努力地推动我们。仅从他在起跑线上的身体语言来看，当他戴上头盔，坐进车里，他正在为战斗做准备。那里充满了激情，充满了动力，对于一个经验丰富的车手来说，这确实是非常令人印象深刻的。
“同时，我们也在从他的反馈和作为一名经验丰富的车手的角度获取他的意见。所以，是的，这是一个非常好的组合。
“很抱歉，第二个问题是关于埃斯特班·奥康的？嗯，看吧，作为一个车队负责人，我相信我的同事也是一样，你会接到来自市场上每一位车手或车手经理的电话和联系。所以，有很多车手和经理已经联系了我。
“我不会说是谁或不是谁，但几乎所有在市场上的人都已经联系过了，正如你所预期的。但是，是的，我想这是最后一个地方，正如你可以想象的那样，我不会在这里传达任何关于车手阵容的信息。
如果威廉·莎士比亚在场，毫无疑问他会拿起羽毛笔在羊皮纸上划掉一条笔记，表示这位绅士过于抗议。幸运的是，对于凯迪拉克车队负责人来说，也许，阿德里安·纽维在场，并成为了后续大多数问题的自然磁铁。
Motorsport.com了解到，奥康几乎不可能加入凯迪拉克，因为他和佩雷斯在上一次同处一室时就像油和水一样不相容。据信他可能会成为阿斯顿·马丁的第三位车手。
凯迪拉克是否会在2027年保留博塔斯，目前尚不清楚，但众所周知，车队老板希望尽快有一位美国车手坐在赛车座位上。洛夫顿今年夏天的意外替代者表明，通用汽车和TWG赛车运动公司的期望似乎领先于车队目前的进展。
凯迪拉克在美洲赛车场的自由练习1中使用了科尔顿·赫塔，但他由于国际汽联改变了资格赛规则，只差一分未能获得超级驾照，因此他成为任何比赛机会的左翼候选人。如果他今年在其他练习中能有有意义的驾驶表现，他将获得资格——但他在本赛季的F2赛事表现相当不稳定，并不是一张很强的名片。
“显然，在美国车队中有美国车手是一个很好的故事，”布德科维茨在本周末对天空体育说。
“这需要是正确的时间和正确的车手。但我们正在努力。我们正在和科尔顿一起努力。
“有一些真正令人兴奋的美国新秀正在崛起。我们看到了Ugo Ugochukwu赢得了F3冠军。我们还有Sebastian Wheldon将在明年进入F3。”
““所以这里有很多潜力，我们当然会去调查。”"
detailEn: Why Cadillac F1 boss provoked fresh intrigue by dodging driver question
Speculation continues to surround the future of Valtteri Bottas at Cadillac as the team looks to bring on an American driver
Marcin Budkowski, Cadillac Team Principal

The US GP weekend naturally means the spotlight gravitates towards Formula 1’s two American-owned teams. That has led to some awkward questions for Cadillac amid ongoing speculation over its driver line-up for 2027 and beyond.

Both Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas are on “multi-year” contracts, understood to be a so-called one-plus-one arrangement in which the second year is optional, subject to either party fulfilling various conditions. Such has been the disparity in performance between the two drivers that Bottas’s position has been the object of paddock gossip for months.

Recently appointed team principal Marcin Budkowski has already had to do some firefighting on this, as had his predecessor Graeme Lowdon. But a rather peculiar moment in the FIA’s press conference for team representatives on Friday in Austin suggested Cadillac’s plans aren’t as fixed as previously billed.

The catalyst was a soft question from one of the broadcasters on the theme of Perez’s upcoming 300th grand prix start: “How difficult is it to evaluate a driver who’s fighting at the back of the grid, at the same time as the impression is that he’s having a better season than his team-mate? And quickly on drivers, would you be interested in having any conversation with Esteban [Ocon] regarding maybe a reserve role?”
In trying to give a suitably anodyne non-answer, Budkowski began to flounder.

“Look, for a driver like Checo, who, as you said, has a huge amount of experience and a number of races, I can tell you he doesn’t behave or drive like a driver who is anywhere close to retirement,” hew said.

“He’s pushing very hard behind the wheel. He’s pushing us very hard also behind the scenes, in the debrief rooms and outside, and regularly texting me and other members of the team to push us to improve. He’s hungry, he’s motivated, and that’s actually really good to see. He does it in his own style.

“We have two drivers: one is more hot and one is probably more cold, if we could say, from there. And they both push the team in their own particular ways, but Checo is, yes, pushing us very hard. And just looking at the way his body language on the grid, when he gets his helmet on and he gets in the car, he’s getting ready for a fight. There’s a lot of fire, there’s a lot of motivation there, so it’s really impressive for a driver of this experience.
“And at the same time, we’re getting his feedback and his input in terms of, as an experienced driver. So yes, it’s a very good combination.

“And sorry, the second question was about Esteban Ocon? Well, look, as a team principal, and I’m sure it’s the same with my colleagues, you’re getting calls and contacts from every driver or driver manager that is on the market. So, there are a number of drivers and managers who have contacted me.

“I’m not going to say who it is or who it isn’t, but pretty much all of them that are on the market have been in touch, as you’d expect. But yes, I think it’s the last place here, as you can imagine, where I would communicate anything on driver line-up.”

Were William Shakespeare present, he would no doubt have put quill to parchment and scratched out a note to the effect that the gentleman doth protest too much. Fortunately for the Cadillac team principal, perhaps, Adrian Newey was in the room and acted as a natural magnet for the majority of further questions.

Motorsport.com understands that Ocon is highly unlikely to go to Cadillac, since he and Perez mixed like oil and water when they last coexisted under the same roof. It’s believed he will probably become Aston Martin’s third driver.

Whether or not Cadillac retain Bottas for 2027, it’s known that the team’s owners wish to have an American driver in a race seat as soon as possible. Lowdon’s surprise replacement this summer is an indication of how General Motors and TWG Motorsports’ expectations appear to be running somewhere ahead of the team’s current progress.

Cadillac ran Colton Herta in FP1 at the Circuit of The Americas, but he is a leftfield candidate for any race opportunities since he is one point short of qualifying for a superlicence, owing to the FIA having changed the qualifying rubric. If he has meaningful running in another session this year he will qualify – but his rather patchy Formula 2 campaign this season isn’t a very strong calling card.
“Obviously having an American driver in an American team is a great story,” Budkowski told Sky Sports this weekend.
“It needs to be the right time and the right driver. But we're working on that. We're working on that with Colton.
“There are some really exciting American talents coming up through the ranks as well. We've seen Ugo Ugochukwu winning F3. We've got [Sebastian] Wheldon coming through to F3 next year.
“So there's a lot of potential here and we'll look into that obviously.”
